data.name: Cassiopeia
data.gender_notes: Cassiopeia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Cassiopeia was a vain queen who boasted that she was more beautiful than the sea goddesses. As punishment, she was transformed into a constellation in the shape of a W or M. The name Cassiopeia carries the meaning “Vanity, boastfulness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cassiopeia usually hope their child will grow to embody vanity, boastfulness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the danger of pride and vanity
data.etymology: Cassiopeia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Vanity, boastfulness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cassiopeia total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: קסיופאיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קסיופאיה היא שם נשי יווני-עברי שמקורו במיתולוגיה היוונית, שפירושו 'מלכה' או 'שליטה'. בברית החדשה, אין מקור ישראלי, אך ישנן ראיות כי קסיופאיה הייתה שם נפוץ בקרב התלמודים היוונים. במהלך השנים, שם זה הפך לסמל לשקרנות ולחסר אמת. בפסוק תהילים 119:163, נאמר 'ה' - 'קסיופאיה' - 'השקר. כי כדורי. ב-1971, הקסיופאיה הוכרזה כקבוצת כוכבים.

in_greek.name: Κασσιопεία
in_greek.long_meaning: Κασσιόπεια (Κασσιόπη, Κασσιόπηα) είναι το όνομα μιας γυναικείας φιγούρας στην ελληνική μυθολογία. Ο ορισμός της αναφέρει ότι ήταν μια βασιλική γυναίκα από την Αιθιοπία που έγινε γοητευτική στην ομορφιά της. Μετά από μια μακρά ιστορία, ο πατέρας της έδωσε την κόρη του, την Κασσιόπη, σε ένα θρανίο. Η Κασσιόπη έφυγε από το θρανίο και έπεσε σε ένα δαχτυλίδι. Ο πατέρας της την έβλεπε από το δαχτυλίδι. Ο πατέρας της, ο ομηρικός βασιλιάς, έστειλε την Κασσιόπη στη Σικελία.

in_latin.name: Cassiopeia
in_latin.long_meaning: Cassiopeia, etymologicamente, significa 'regina' o 'sovrana', ma nel corso dei secoli, il nome è stato associato alla figura della regina di Etiopia, nota per la sua bellezza e la sua falsità. Nell'antica Grecia, il nome veniva usato per descrivere una figura femminile nota per la sua vanità e la sua falsità. Nella Bibbia, il nome non è presente, ma nel Nuovo Testamento, si fa riferimento a una donna che si è comportata in modo simile a quella di Cassiopeia. Nell'ambito della Chiesa cristiana, il nome è stato associato alla figura della donna che si è comportata in modo simile a quella di Cassiopeia, ovvero una donna che ha espresso un'opinione falsa circa il Signore.

in_english.name: Cassiopeia
in_english.meaning: Queen of the Sea, associated with falsehood and vanity
in_english.long_meaning: Cassiopeia is a female given name with roots in Greek mythology. The name is derived from the word 'kassios' meaning 'sea' and 'peia' meaning 'she who rules'. In the Bible, Cassiopeia is not mentioned, but in the New Testament, it is referred to as a false statement made by a woman. In Christian tradition, the name is associated with the figure of a woman who has expressed a false opinion about the Lord. The name has also been associated with the constellation Cassiopeia, named after the queen in Greek mythology.

data.cultural_impact: The constellation Cassiopeia has been recognized by cultures throughout history and is visible all around the world. It is often associated with royalty and vanity due to the origins of the mythological queen.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Cassiopeia can serve as a reminder of the dangers of pride and vanity. The story of the queen who boasted of her beauty and was punished by being transformed into a constellation can be seen as a cautionary tale about the dangers of pride and the importance of humility. Additionally, the constellation's shape can be seen as a reminder of the cross, representing the sacrifice and humility of Jesus Christ.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cassiopeia, in Greek mythology, was a vain queen whose boastfulness led to her being punished by the gods and transformed into a constellation in the form of a W shaped queen, a reminder of the dangers of pride and hubris. In Christianity, this symbolizes the importance of humility and the potential consequences of arrogance.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Cassiopeia was a queen of Ethiopia, famous for her vanity. The name Cassiopeia carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Cassiopeia remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Cassiopeia, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Cassiopeia meaning "Vanity, boastfulness" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
